```{ojs}
viewof sg = Inputs.select(["all", ...SGROUPS.map(s => s.k)], {format: k => SGL[k], value: param("sg", "all"), label: "Sector group"})
viewof ov = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Staff per 1,000 students", "lvl"], ["Change in staff (log points)", "chg"]]), {value: param("view", "lvl"), label: "Show"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  setParam("sg", sg === "all" ? null : sg); setParam("view", ov === "lvl" ? null : ov);

      marks: [Plot.link(sub, {y1: "l", y2: "l", x1: "per1000_fy2015", x2: "per1000_fy2024", stroke: d => d.ef ? c : GRAY, strokeWidth: 3, markerEnd: "arrow"}),

    })}<p class="cs-note">Open circle: FY2015; arrow tip: FY2024. Colored: enrollment-facing groups. ${SGL[sg]}, ${rows[0].n} institutions; all staff ${f1(rows.find(d => d.occ === "allstaff").per1000_fy2015)} → ${f1(rows.find(d => d.occ === "allstaff").per1000_fy2024)} per 1,000.</p>`;
  }
  const fte = rows[0].dlog_fte;
  return html`${Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 900), height: 40 + rows.length * 32, marginLeft: narrow ? 150 : 380, marginRight: 95,
    x: {grid: true, insetLeft: 36, insetRight: 36, label: "Change in FTE staff, FY2015–24 (log points ×100)"}, y: {domain: order, label: null, tickFormat: l => narrow ? l.trim().split(" (")[0] : l},
    marks: [Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: INK}), Plot.ruleX([fte], {stroke: BREAKC, strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
      Plot.barX(rows, {y: "l", x: "dlog", fill: d => d.ef ? c : d.occ === "allstaff" ? INK : LIGHT, rx: 2}),
      Plot.text(rows.filter(d => d.dlog < 0), {y: "l", x: "dlog", text: d => s1(d.dlog), dx: -4, textAnchor: "end", fontSize: 10, fill: INK}),
      Plot.text(rows.filter(d => d.dlog >= 0), {y: "l", x: "dlog", text: d => s1(d.dlog), dx: 4, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10, fill: INK}),
      Plot.text([fte], {x: d => d, frameAnchor: "top", text: d => `students ${s1(d)}`, dy: -4, fill: BREAKC, fontSize: 10})]
  })}<p class="cs-note">Red dashed line: the change in fall FTE students. A group whose bar lies to the right of the line grew per student.</p>`;
}
```

::: {.cs-note}
**Data.** IPEDS Human Resources occupation codes (the detailed categories exist from fall 2012), non-medical staff, FTE = full-time + one-third of part-time; S11 surviving institutions; FY2015 base, because student-affairs staff (code 270) jump 22–24% in FY2014 as reporting settled; a FY2016 base gives the same split. Mean of institution ratios. FY2024 NCES provisional.
:::

## Instructional and non-instructional staff

Occupation codes split staff into instruction and everything else. The default shows both, in FTE (full-time + one-third of part-time), FY2015 → FY2024, per 1,000 students. Instruction (IPEDS code 210) is close to, but not the same as, faculty: research and public-service staff with faculty status count as non-instructional here.

```{ojs}
viewof dmo = Inputs.select(new Map([["Instructional and non-instructional FTE", "pair"], ["Full-time headcount", "ft"], ["Part-time headcount", "pt"]]), {value: ["pair", "ft", "pt"].includes(param("dm", "pair")) ? param("dm", "pair") : "pair", label: "Staff measure"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  setParam("dm", dmo === "pair" ? null : dmo);

"FTE staff" : "Staff (headcount)"} per 1,000 FTE students, FY2015 → FY2024`}, fy: {domain: order.map(k => SGL[k]), label: null}, y: {domain: OC2.map(d => d[1]), label: null, axis: narrow ? null : "left", tickFormat: l => l.replace(", full-time", "").replace(", part-time", "")},
    marks: [Plot.link(rows, {fy: "gl", y1: "l", y2: "l", x1: "per1000_fy2015", x2: "per1000_fy2024", stroke: d => d.occ.startsWith("instr") ? GRAY : SGC[d.sg], strokeWidth: 3, markerEnd: "arrow"}),
      Plot.dot(rows, {fy: "gl", y: "l", x: "per1000_fy2015", r: 4, fill: "white", stroke: GRAY, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.text(rows, {fy: "gl", y: "l", x: d => Math.max(d.per1000_fy2015, d.per1000_fy2024), text: d => `${f1(d.per1000_fy2015)} → ${f1(d.per1000_fy2024)}`, dx: 8, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10, fill: INK}),
      Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointerY({fy: "gl", y: "l", x: "per1000_fy2024", title: d => `${d.gl}: ${d.l}\nper 1,000: ${f1(d.per1000_fy2015)} (FY2015) → ${f1(d.per1000_fy2024)} (FY2024)\n${d.n} institutions`}))]

  ${order.map(sg => { const d = EF.find(x => x.sg === sg); return d ? html`<tr><td>${SGL[sg]}</td><td>${s1(d.d_noninstr)}</td><td>${s1(d.d_enrfacing)}</td><td><b>${sg === "xr" ? "n/a" : pct0(d.share_of_noninstr_rise)}</b></td><td>${sg === "xr" ? "n/a" : pct0(d.share_of_allstaff_rise_v1)}</td></tr>` : ""; })}
  </tbody></table></div>
  <p class="cs-note">Open circle: FY2015; arrow tip: FY2024. S11 surviving institutions, non-medical staff, mean of institution ratios. Private research: non-instructional staff per 1,000 rose only ${f1(EF.find(d => d.sg === "xr")?.d_noninstr)}, so a share of that rise is not meaningful. ${(() => { const c = OC.find(d => d.sg === "cc" && d.occ === "instr_pt"); return c ? `At community colleges part-time instructors per 1,000 students fell (${f1(c.per1000_fy2015)} → ${f1(c.per1000_fy2024)}): adjuncts were cut faster than enrollment fell.` : ""; })()}</p>`;
}
```

## Enrollment-facing staff don't track enrollment

```{ojs}
{
  const EL3 = {instr: "Instruction (FTE)", instr_ft: "Instruction, full-time", noninstr: "Non-instructional (FTE)", enrfacing: "Enrollment-facing", allstaff: "All non-medical staff"};
  const keep = Object.keys(EL3);
  const r = OE.filter(d => keep.includes(d.occ) && d.sg === "all").map(d => ({...d, l: EL3[d.occ], lo: d.iv - 1.96 * d.iv_se, hi: d.iv + 1.96 * d.iv_se}));
  return html`${Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 760), height: 230, marginLeft: 170, marginRight: 60,
    x: {grid: true, domain: [-0.3, 1.4], label: "Elasticity to fall FTE, gravity instrument (95% interval)"}, y: {domain: Object.values(EL3), label: null},
    marks: [Plot.ruleX([1], {stroke: BREAKC, strokeDasharray: "4,3"}), Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#bbb"}),
      Plot.ruleY(r, {y: "l", x1: "lo", x2: "hi", stroke: BLUE, strokeWidth: 3}), Plot.dot(r, {y: "l", x: "iv", r: 6, fill: BLUE, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.text(r, {y: "l", x: "hi", text: d => f2(d.iv), dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fill: INK})]
  })}<p class="cs-note">Pooled across sectors, gravity population instrument (base 2002), FY2015–24. Enrollment-facing staff move about ${f2(r.find(d => d.occ === "enrfacing").iv)} with enrollment, only slightly less than non-instructional staff as a whole (${f2(r.find(d => d.occ === "noninstr").iv)}) and about the same as full-time instructional staff (${f2(r.find(d => d.occ === "instr_ft").iv)}). Instructional FTE (${f2(r.find(d => d.occ === "instr").iv)}) responds more, mostly through part-time instructors. Intervals are wide. Growth in enrollment-facing staff over FY2015–19 also does not predict first-time enrollment over FY2019–24 (see the payoff table on <a href="../amenities-athletics/index.html#payoff">Amenities and athletics</a>).</p>`;
}
```

## Coaches

IPEDS has no code for coaches; they sit inside "counseling, arts, sports and media." Subtracting coach FTE reported to the Equity in Athletics survey shows how much of the enrollment-facing growth is coaching.

```{ojs}
{
  const r = CO.map(d => ({...d, l: SGL[d.sg]}));
  const order = ["all", ...SGROUPS.map(s => s.k)].map(k => SGL[k]);
  return html`${Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 820), height: 60 + order.length * 34, marginLeft: 200, marginRight: 60,
    x: {domain: [0, 0.7], tickFormat: "%", grid: true, label: "Coaches' share of growth in enrollment-facing staff, FY2015–24"}, y: {domain: order, label: null},
    marks: [Plot.barX(r, {y: "l", x: "coach_share_of_enrfacing_growth", fill: d => SGC[d.sg], rx: 2}),
      Plot.text(r, {y: "l", x: "coach_share_of_enrfacing_growth", text: d => pct0(d.coach_share_of_enrfacing_growth), dx: 5, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fill: INK}),
      Plot.tip(r, Plot.pointerY({y: "l", x: "coach_share_of_enrfacing_growth", title: d => `${d.l}\nenrollment-facing FTE +${f0(d.d_enrfacing_total)}, of which coaches +${f0(d.d_coach_fte_total)}\nper 1,000 students: +${f1(d.d_enrfacing_per1000)}, coaches +${f1(d.d_coach_fte_per1000)}\n${d.n} institutions`}))]
  })}<p class="cs-note">Lower bounds on athletics staffing: athletic directors and administrators, trainers and sports-information staff are not counted as coaches. Share of the growth in total enrollment-facing FTE across the group's institutions. Source: IPEDS Human Resources; Equity in Athletics Data Analysis (EADA) coach FTE.</p>`;
}
```
